title: CuTe DSL Code Generation for GPU Kernels
critical_patterns: Use preprocessor=True for functions with loops or conditionals
Tracing-only mode is suitable for simple arithmetic operations without control flow
AST Rewriting captures entire program structure for optimization
Tracing records operations during execution with proxy arguments
constraints: Preprocessor mode requires a well-defined subset of Python
Tracing mode loses untaken branches and unrolls loops to specific iteration counts
Preprocessor mode is the default and recommended for most use cases
Tracing mode is fragile and should be used with caution
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL converts Python code into optimized GPU kernels using two main techniques: AST Rewriting and Tracing. AST Rewriting analyzes the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) of a function before execution to capture control flow structures such as loops and conditionals, converting them into structured Intermediate Representation (IR). This method enables optimizations like loop tiling, vectorization, and correct handling of all valid inputs, but requires adherence to a supported subset of Python syntax. Tracing, on the other hand, records operations during a single execution with 'proxy' arguments, producing a flat sequence of operations. While this method offers near-zero compile latency and supports many Python features, it fails to preserve control flow structures, making it unsuitable for functions with loops or conditionals. CuTe DSL provides two modes: Tracing Only (preprocessor=False) and Preprocessor Mode (preprocessor=True). The default Preprocessor Mode combines AST Rewriting and Tracing, ensuring correct and optimized code generation for complex kernels. Tracing Only mode is limited to simple arithmetic operations without control flow and should be used only when absolute fastest compilation is needed. Common misconceptions include the belief that Tracing is always faster or that Preprocessor Mode limits Python usage. In reality, Preprocessor Mode provides robust correctness and optimization, essential for most GPU kernels. Debugging tools such as IR dumping and verbose logging can assist in resolving code generation issues. Overall, the recommendation is to use Preprocessor Mode for all but the simplest arithmetic-only functions.
